sections_target.text: This document sets out the steps for compressing Mid Span Joints for steel-reinforced aluminium conductors (ACSR) on overhead lines using the hydraulic press instead of the parallel clamps used in welding the conductors.

The document was reviewed by the general managers of overhead lines in the regions of the Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company and the MPIS coordinators of the electricity distribution companies.

rows: A work order must be issued including the names of the workers, and they must have occupational safety and health category cards.
Occupational safety and health equipment must be used, such as a safety helmet, safety shoes, cotton overalls, etc.
No more than one mid-span joint shall be made in one phase of one span.
Joints are prohibited at the following crossings: above railways, the River Nile, navigable canals, main roads, electricity and telephone lines, etc.
Mid-span joints shall be at a distance greater than 30 m from the suspension or tension clamp (for high and extra high voltage).

Do not load the weight of the conductor on the sleeve (joint/ferrule) during each compression, to ensure the joint stays straight and does not bend, especially when making the first compression; in general the conductor and the sleeve shall be horizontal and in one straight line during compression.
Comply with the manufacturer's instructions regarding the number of compressions and the distances between them.
Occupational safety and health equipment such as protective goggles, safety helmet, cotton overalls, etc.
A suitable compression press for the joints and the dies suitable for the joint section and type, as per the manufacturer's recommendation.
Hacksaw, adhesive tape, suitable solvent, cloth, cloth sandpaper, metal brush 0.2 to 0.3 mm long.
A special file for removing and chamfering excess material, protrusions or joint burrs and smoothing them.
Make sure the dies for steel and aluminium represent the required size.
Make sure the inner diameters of the ends (steel and aluminium) are clean.
Make sure the conductor end is sound; if damaged, cut off the damaged part.
Insert the conductor into the end of the joint and let it slide in to about 1 metre.

Bind the conductor with metal wire or suitable adhesive tape up to about 3 cm from the end, then cut the aluminium ends near the adhesive tape with a hacksaw, taking care not to nick the steel wires (Figure x1a).
Bind the ends of the conductors (Figure x1b).
Bind the conductor with adhesive tape at a distance from the end of the conductor equal to (half the length of the steel joint + 15%).

Cut the aluminium wires at the end of the adhesive tape (Figure x1c), taking care not to nick the wires; to avoid this, cut with the hacksaw the outer layer of the conductor and cut only about 2/3 of the diameter of the aluminium wires of the inner layer, which will be removed by repeated bending.

Put a reference mark on the core with the aluminium wires at a distance equal to half the length of the steel joint. Put the core inside the steel joint at a distance of 2 cm, then insert the core up to the mark made previously. To carry out this operation, hold the joint by compressing it in the die placed on the press.
Repeat the operations mentioned in steps 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 on the other conductor end to be joined, and make sure the steel joint is in the position shown in Figure x1d.

Compress the steel joint starting from the centre (Figure x1d), starting from the first end, then the other end, and make sure the core is inserted to the middle of the joint, making sure of the appropriate pressure value shown on the pressure gauge.

Make sure all the aluminium wires of the conductor to be compressed are clean; if the conductor is greased or blackened, use a suitable solvent, and if it is old, use cloth sandpaper or a metal brush with steel wire 0.2 to 0.3 mm long.

Starting from the centre of the steel joint, put a reference mark on each conductor at a distance equal to half the length of the aluminium joint. Let the conductor slide inside the steel joint, remove the adhesive tape and stop at the mark made, and make sure the centre of the aluminium joint is in the same place as the centre of the steel joint.
Compress the joint starting from the mark <--I on the sleeve, at the start of the aluminium conductor (Figure x1e), and follow step 11.

Introduction
This document sets out the steps for compressing Mid Span Joints for steel-reinforced aluminium conductors (ACSR) on overhead lines using the hydraulic press instead of the parallel clamps used in welding the conductors.
The document was reviewed by the general managers of overhead lines in the regions of the Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company and the MPIS coordinators of the electricity distribution companies.
Safety Precautions
A work order must be issued including the names of the workers, and they must have occupational safety and health category cards. | 
Occupational safety and health equipment must be used, such as a safety helmet, safety shoes, cotton overalls, etc. | 
The following shall be observed:
No more than one mid-span joint shall be made in one phase of one span. | 
Joints are prohibited at the following crossings: above railways, the River Nile, navigable canals, main roads, electricity and telephone lines, etc. | 
Mid-span joints shall be at a distance greater than 30 m from the suspension or tension clamp (for high and extra high voltage). | 
Do not load the weight of the conductor on the sleeve (joint/ferrule) during each compression, to ensure the joint stays straight and does not bend, especially when making the first compression; in general the conductor and the sleeve shall be horizontal and in one straight line during compression. | 
Comply with the manufacturer's instructions regarding the number of compressions and the distances between them. | 
Tools, Instruments and Equipment Used
Occupational safety and health equipment such as protective goggles, safety helmet, cotton overalls, etc. | 
A suitable compression press for the joints and the dies suitable for the joint section and type, as per the manufacturer's recommendation. | 
Hacksaw, adhesive tape, suitable solvent, cloth, cloth sandpaper, metal brush 0.2 to 0.3 mm long. | 
A special file for removing and chamfering excess material, protrusions or joint burrs and smoothing them. | 
Procedures to be Carried Out
Make sure the dies for steel and aluminium represent the required size. | 1.
Make sure the inner diameters of the ends (steel and aluminium) are clean. | 2.

Bind the ends of the conductors (Figure x1b). | 6.
Bind the conductor with adhesive tape at a distance from the end of the conductor equal to (half the length of the steel joint + 15%). | 7.

Put a reference mark on the core with the aluminium wires at a distance equal to half the length of the steel joint. Put the core inside the steel joint at a distance of 2 cm, then insert the core up to the mark made previously. To carry out this operation, hold the joint by compressing it in the die placed on the press. | 9.
Repeat the operations mentioned in steps 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 on the other conductor end to be joined, and make sure the steel joint is in the position shown in Figure x1d. | 10.

Make sure all the aluminium wires of the conductor to be compressed are clean; if the conductor is greased or blackened, use a suitable solvent, and if it is old, use cloth sandpaper or a metal brush with steel wire 0.2 to 0.3 mm long. | 12.
Starting from the centre of the steel joint, put a reference mark on each conductor at a distance equal to half the length of the aluminium joint. Let the conductor slide inside the steel joint, remove the adhesive tape and stop at the mark made, and make sure the centre of the aluminium joint is in the same place as the centre of the steel joint. | 13.
Compress the joint starting from the mark <--I on the sleeve, at the start of the aluminium conductor (Figure x1e), and follow step 11. | 14.
